main.title: Jensen Huang wraps up South Korea visit, stresses physical AI cooperation and startup support
main.body: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang concluded his five-day South Korea visit on June 9, 2026. At the Korea AI Ecosystem Reception on June 8 at the Shilla Hotel, Huang stated: "South Korea is a country unmatched in heavy industry, manufacturing, electronics and AI software." He predicted "hundreds of billions of dollars in revenue will flow into South Korea" over the next five years. Huang urged venture capital firms to invest in AI startups by name, and requested government-level funding support from Deputy Prime Minister Bae Kyung-hoon. South Korea was identified as Nvidia's top physical AI partner outside the United States, with companies like Doosan Robotics, RealWorld, Arobot, and Robotis participating. Government agreements with Deputy PM Bae included: prioritized supply of next-generation Vera Rubin accelerators; priority support for 260,000 existing GPU units; positive reception to hosting GTC Korea; and GPU pricing benefit discussions. For memory: Samsung Electronics discussed HBM supply, foundry cooperation, and next-generation memory through HBM5. SK Hynix was praised with Huang noting "very big results this year" with anticipated growth in H2 and 2027. Infrastructure: Naver targeting 55MW by 2027, scaling to 200MW in 2028, targeting GW-class. SK Telecom building up to 5 GW AI factory on Nvidia DSX. Five universities invited: KAIST, UNIST, SNU, Korea University, and POSTECH. Nvidia AI Technology Center hiring underway in Korea.

main.title: Nvidia and SK Hynix seal multi-year HBM4 AI memory deal
main.body: Nvidia and SK Hynix announced a multi-year co-development partnership covering the design and manufacture of next-generation memory chips for artificial intelligence systems. The agreement was unveiled during Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's tour of South Korea and gives SK Hynix a formal role in developing high-bandwidth memory for Nvidia's most advanced accelerators, particularly the Vera Rubin platform entering full production. The deal extends beyond standard supply arrangements: both companies will jointly develop memory infrastructure specifically designed for AI factories — large-scale data center clusters used for training and inference operations. The partnership covers physical AI applications and memory tailored for Vera Rubin. Vera Rubin systems integrate clusters of Vera central processing units and Rubin graphics cores alongside terabytes of HBM4 memory. The platform delivers approximately 3.5 times the training performance and five times the inference performance compared to its Blackwell predecessor. Production shipments commence in Q3 2026. Memory has emerged as the industry's critical bottleneck. Arm CEO Rene Haas characterized memory as "probably the toughest" constraint facing the sector. The memory supercycle is projected to persist through at least 2028, with some forecasts extending shortages to 2030. SK Hynix controls approximately 60-70% of HBM4 volume for Vera Rubin; Samsung holds 25-30%; Micron supplies the remainder. The multi-year agreement strengthens SK Hynix's position, enabling capacity expansion and market share consolidation. SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-Won stated: "Together, we are co-developing the next generation of memory for AI factories and applying AI to how we design and manufacture semiconductors." SK Group plans to launch a gigawatt-class AI factory in Korea next year.

main.title: Samsung memory chief, Nvidia CEO discuss next-generation HBM cooperation
main.body: Samsung Electronics vice chairman Jun Young-hyun met with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on June 8, 2026, at a hotel in Seoul to discuss long-term cooperation on advanced memory technologies and foundry business. Jun stated: "We have maintained cooperation with CEO Huang for a long period, and we have had very productive discussions so far." The meeting focused on near-term supply of HBM4 and SOCAMM products this year, as well as longer-term joint development of HBM4E and HBM5 technologies starting next year. Foundry cooperation was also discussed, with Samsung currently manufacturing NVIDIA's Groq LP30 inference processor at its 4-nanometer process, and Jun confirming Samsung will also handle the next-generation LP40. When asked about Nvidia's stated preference for SK Hynix as its primary memory partner, Jun responded that Samsung would "work hard on what we do" and demonstrate results through performance. Industry analysts project SK Hynix will capture between 60–70% of the HBM4 supply volume for Vera Rubin, while Samsung secures 25–30%, leaving Micron with the balance. HBM chips are specialized memory semiconductors that pair with AI processors to deliver the bandwidth necessary for AI training and inference operations. Samsung aims to strengthen its position in the expanding HBM market.

main.title: NVIDIA and LG Group Build an AI Factory to Advance Physical AI, Mobility and AI Infrastructure
main.body: NVIDIA and LG Group are partnering to build an AI factory to accelerate LG Group's next wave of AI-driven businesses, spanning robotics, autonomous driving, data center technologies and GPU cloud services. LG Uplus plans to build a large-scale AI data center capable of accommodating the latest NVIDIA GPUs. LG's 200MW data center in Paju, Gyeonggi Province, is due live in 2027. The collaboration emphasizes physical AI and robotics: LG can integrate NVIDIA Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab robotics frameworks into development workflows to simulate, train and validate home cobots in physically accurate virtual environments. LG Electronics is developing a physical AI data factory to help Korean and global companies accelerate physical AI projects. LG AI Research used NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs, NVIDIA NeMo framework and NVIDIA Nemotron open datasets to support EXAONE model development, as well as NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM software for high-performance inference. The announcement was made on June 7-8, 2026, during NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's visit to South Korea. NVIDIA's Isaac GR00T foundation model will be used for LG's home cobot development. This partnership covers M.A.P.: Mobility, AI Infrastructure, and Physical AI.

main.title: OpenAI files confidentially for IPO, following Anthropic
main.body: OpenAI submitted a confidential draft registration statement to the SEC for a proposed IPO. The company announced this proactively through its official blog, stating: "We recently submitted a confidential S-1. We expect it to leak so we're just announcing it." The company indicated it has "not decided on timing yet; it may be a while because there are things we want to do that are likely easier as a private company. But it's a complicated set of tradeoffs, and this gives us the option to go public sooner if that ends up being best." OpenAI is working with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley on a potential listing as soon as the fall. The company is currently valued at $852 billion post-money (March 2026 valuation). This filing follows Anthropic's IPO submission by just over a week. SpaceX is also expected to debut at a $1.75 trillion valuation. OpenAI faces significant headwinds: the company recently missed user and revenue targets. Projections indicate the firm will burn approximately $85 billion in 2028 despite doubling sales, meaning it won't generate positive cash flow for at least four more years. Data center spending alone is expected to reach $122 billion annually. OpenAI boasts approximately 900 million weekly active users globally. CEO Sam Altman told CNBC the company will proceed "when appropriate timing arrives." The filing momentum accelerated following OpenAI's legal victory against Elon Musk last month.

main.title: Elon Musk In Direct Talks With ASML For $119B TeraFab Chip Plant: CEO Calls Him 'Very Serious'
main.body: Elon Musk is in direct negotiations with ASML regarding a proposed semiconductor manufacturing facility called TeraFab in Texas. ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet confirmed the discussions, describing Musk as "very serious about all those projects," which encompass semiconductor ventures and satellite ambitions connected to Tesla, xAI, and SpaceX. TeraFab is a vertically integrated semiconductor project announced March 21, 2026, as a joint effort between Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI. Intel is contributing 14A process technology. The facility is planned for Grimes County, Texas, with an initial investment of $55 billion and total projected costs up to $119 billion. Fouquet on market conditions: "Demand on AI is coming so strongly that we will be in a supply-limited market for quite a while." Fouquet on market projections: "The global semiconductor market could eventually reach $1.5 trillion by 2030 as AI-related demand accelerates." ASML CEO Fouquet and Musk had conversations about TeraFab reportedly in May 2026. Musk is scheduled to appear virtually at ASML's private annual technology conference on June 9-10, joining CEO Fouquet for a fireside chat about TeraFab. ASML, headquartered in the Netherlands, is the world's sole manufacturer of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines. Without ASML's machines, TeraFab cannot function. ASML shares rose 5.81% on June 8, 2026, after Musk publicly described ASML as "arguably the greatest company in Europe." ASML's market cap reached $674 billion, making it Europe's most valuable company in history.

main.title: Demand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsible — why the CPU to GPU ratio is more important than ever for hyperscalers
main.body: The rise of agentic AI is causing data center CPU demand to surge, reversing the historical GPU-dominated ratio. Historically, AI deployments favored a 4:1 to 8:1 GPU-to-CPU ratio for chatbot workloads. As agentic AI becomes dominant, this balance is reversing significantly. CPUs now handle critical functions including orchestration, memory management, networking, storage coordination, and inference handling. AMD reports CPU market growth has doubled from an anticipated 18% annual rate to 35% annually, projecting the sector to reach $120 billion by decade's end. Rather than dense GPU configurations with minimal CPU support, hyperscalers now deploy higher core-count CPUs with expanded memory channels. Some deployments use multiple CPUs per node to manage data movement demands. Agentic AI systems require sustained, high-load CPU operation for continuous, multi-step reasoning — unlike brief GPU inference bursts in chatbot scenarios. CPUs currently account for approximately 91% of latency in AI response times, making them critical optimization targets. Arm-based custom processors dominate hyperscaler deployments, with approximately half of all hyperscaler compute based on Arm architecture in 2025, including AWS Graviton, Google Axion, and Microsoft Cobalt chips. The shift has major implications for data center design: racks are being re-engineered to balance GPU and CPU density.

competitor_articles.title: Nvidia and SK Hynix seal multi-year HBM4 AI memory deal
competitor_articles.body: Nvidia and SK Hynix announced a multi-year co-development partnership covering the design and manufacture of next-generation memory chips for artificial intelligence systems. The agreement was unveiled during Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's tour of South Korea and gives SK Hynix a formal role in developing high-bandwidth memory for Nvidia's most advanced accelerators, particularly the Vera Rubin platform entering full production. The deal extends beyond standard supply arrangements: both companies will jointly develop memory infrastructure specifically designed for AI factories — large-scale data center clusters used for training and inference operations. The partnership covers physical AI applications and memory tailored for Vera Rubin. Vera Rubin systems integrate clusters of Vera central processing units and Rubin graphics cores alongside terabytes of HBM4 memory. The platform delivers approximately 3.5 times the training performance and five times the inference performance compared to its Blackwell predecessor. Production shipments commence in Q3 2026. Memory has emerged as the industry's critical bottleneck. Arm CEO Rene Haas characterized memory as "probably the toughest" constraint facing the sector. The memory supercycle is projected to persist through at least 2028, with some forecasts extending shortages to 2030. SK Hynix controls approximately 60-70% of HBM4 volume for Vera Rubin; Samsung holds 25-30%; Micron supplies the remainder. The multi-year agreement strengthens SK Hynix's position, enabling capacity expansion and market share consolidation. SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-Won stated: "Together, we are co-developing the next generation of memory for AI factories and applying AI to how we design and manufacture semiconductors." SK Group plans to launch a gigawatt-class AI factory in Korea next year.

competitor_articles.title: Samsung memory chief, Nvidia CEO discuss next-generation HBM cooperation
competitor_articles.body: Samsung Electronics vice chairman Jun Young-hyun met with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on June 8, 2026, at a hotel in Seoul to discuss long-term cooperation on advanced memory technologies and foundry business. Jun stated: "We have maintained cooperation with CEO Huang for a long period, and we have had very productive discussions so far." The meeting focused on near-term supply of HBM4 and SOCAMM products this year, as well as longer-term joint development of HBM4E and HBM5 technologies starting next year. Foundry cooperation was also discussed, with Samsung currently manufacturing NVIDIA's Groq LP30 inference processor at its 4-nanometer process, and Jun confirming Samsung will also handle the next-generation LP40. When asked about Nvidia's stated preference for SK Hynix as its primary memory partner, Jun responded that Samsung would "work hard on what we do" and demonstrate results through performance. Industry analysts project SK Hynix will capture between 60–70% of the HBM4 supply volume for Vera Rubin, while Samsung secures 25–30%, leaving Micron with the balance. HBM chips are specialized memory semiconductors that pair with AI processors to deliver the bandwidth necessary for AI training and inference operations. Samsung aims to strengthen its position in the expanding HBM market.

competitor_articles.title: Marvell posts record Q1 FY2027 data center revenue — $1.83B, 76% of total
competitor_articles.body: Marvell Technology reported record Q1 FY2027 results with data center revenue surging to $1.83 billion, representing approximately 76% of total revenue. Total revenue grew strongly year-over-year driven by custom AI silicon and AI networking demand. Marvell projected its custom chip business would cross $10 billion in revenue by fiscal 2029, fueled by growing AI data center investment. Jensen Huang's June 2 statement at COMPUTEX calling Marvell 'the next trillion-dollar company' sent the stock up 33% in a single session, reaching a 26-year record. NVIDIA's $2 billion strategic equity investment in Marvell (March 2026) as part of the NVLink Fusion partnership context continues to drive investor confidence. Marvell's Teralynx T100 — the industry-first 102.4 Tbps AI switch chip in 3nm, under 1000W, with 512-port scale-out — entered Q2 2026 sampling. The chip targets the 'data center without distance' vision using co-packaged optics (CPO).

competitor_articles.title: South Korea Holds K-AI Semiconductor Forum to Showcase Domestic AI Chip Commercialization
competitor_articles.body: South Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT hosted the K-AI Semiconductor Growth Forum on June 4, 2026, at Lotte Hotel Seoul to highlight progress in domestic AI semiconductor development. Deputy Prime Minister Bae Kyung-hoon stated that "domestic AI semiconductors are a core foundation for realizing the national goal of becoming one of the world's top three AI powers." The forum brought together AI semiconductor makers, demand companies, and government agencies to share successful commercial use cases. Rebellions presented SK Telecom's A.Dot call summarization service powered by Rebellions chips, and co-developed a real-time water pollution detection service for a UAE energy company. Rebellions' Rebel-100 AI chip underwent K-Perf benchmarking validation. FuriosaAI contributed to maritime surveillance drone and wildfire management platform deployments. FuriosaAI's Renegade processor received K-Perf testing and validation. Samsung SDS uses FuriosaAI processors for subscription-based AI semiconductor services. HyperAccel developed a public complaint analysis service utilizing large language models. Korean AI semiconductor firms secured over $30 million in export contracts across the UK, Taiwan, Vietnam, and China. The forum highlighted demonstration projects including autonomous livestock management systems, wildfire detection platforms, and mobility assistance wheelchairs. NIPA President Park Yun-gyu also attended the event.

competitor_articles.title: NVIDIA and LG Group Build an AI Factory to Advance Physical AI, Mobility and AI Infrastructure
competitor_articles.body: NVIDIA and LG Group are partnering to build an AI factory to accelerate LG Group's next wave of AI-driven businesses, spanning robotics, autonomous driving, data center technologies and GPU cloud services. LG Uplus plans to build a large-scale AI data center capable of accommodating the latest NVIDIA GPUs. LG's 200MW data center in Paju, Gyeonggi Province, is due live in 2027. The collaboration emphasizes physical AI and robotics: LG can integrate NVIDIA Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab robotics frameworks into development workflows to simulate, train and validate home cobots in physically accurate virtual environments. LG Electronics is developing a physical AI data factory to help Korean and global companies accelerate physical AI projects. LG AI Research used NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs, NVIDIA NeMo framework and NVIDIA Nemotron open datasets to support EXAONE model development, as well as NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM software for high-performance inference. The announcement was made on June 7-8, 2026, during NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's visit to South Korea. NVIDIA's Isaac GR00T foundation model will be used for LG/home cobot development. This partnership covers M.A.P.: Mobility, AI Infrastructure, and Physical AI.

competitor_articles.body: Naver Cloud has emerged as one of Nvidia's closest strategic partners in South Korea. Naver Cloud was selected as a preferred partner for South Korea's 2026 AI computing infrastructure project valued at approximately 2 trillion won. competitor_articles.title: Elon Musk In Direct Talks With ASML For $119B TeraFab Chip Plant: CEO Calls Him 'Very Serious'
competitor_articles.body: Elon Musk is in direct negotiations with ASML regarding a proposed semiconductor manufacturing facility called TeraFab in Texas. ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet confirmed the discussions, describing Musk as "very serious about all those projects," which encompass semiconductor ventures and satellite ambitions connected to Tesla, xAI, and SpaceX. TeraFab is a vertically integrated semiconductor project announced March 21, 2026, as a joint effort between Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI. Intel is contributing 14A process technology. The facility is planned for Grimes County, Texas, with an initial investment of $55 billion and total projected costs up to $119 billion. Fouquet on market conditions: "Demand on AI is coming so strongly that we will be in a supply-limited market for quite a while." Fouquet on market projections: "The global semiconductor market could eventually reach $1.5 trillion by 2030 as AI-related demand accelerates." ASML CEO Fouquet and Musk had conversations about TeraFab reportedly in May 2026. Musk is scheduled to appear virtually at ASML's private annual technology conference on June 9-10, joining CEO Fouquet for a fireside chat about TeraFab. ASML, headquartered in the Netherlands, is the world's sole manufacturer of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines. Without ASML's machines, TeraFab cannot function. ASML shares rose 5.81% on June 8, 2026, after Musk publicly described ASML as "arguably the greatest company in Europe." ASML's market cap reached $674 billion, making it Europe's most valuable company in history.

competitor_articles.title: SK Hynix and Nvidia co-developing memory and memory manufacturing tech
competitor_articles.body: SK Hynix and Nvidia announced a multi-year strategic cooperation agreement focused on co-developing memory technology for Nvidia GPU servers, edge RTX Spark workstations, and Jetson robots. SK Hynix will leverage Nvidia software technology for semiconductor factory digital twin simulation and manufacturing optimization using robotics. SK Hynix currently supplies high-bandwidth memory (HBM) to Nvidia for GPUs including Blackwell systems and upcoming Vera Rubin accelerators featuring HBM4 technology. As one of three HBM suppliers alongside Samsung and Micron, SK Hynix is the only company with this strategic partnership arrangement with Nvidia. The partnership elevates the relationship from simple supplier-contractor to a broader alliance. SK Hynix will share memory technology roadmaps with Nvidia and diversify into AI infrastructure, personal AI, and physical AI markets. The collaboration extends beyond Vera Rubin supercomputers to include Vera CPUs, RTX Spark PCs, and Jetson Thor robotic platforms. SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-Won stated: "Together, we are co-developing the next generation of memory for AI factories and applying AI to how we design and manufacture semiconductors" — work expected to shape AI infrastructure development. SK Group plans to launch a gigawatt-class AI factory in Korea next year. Technical collaboration includes SK Hynix using Nvidia's CUDA-X libraries and PhysicsNeMo framework for semiconductor simulation. Additionally, SK Hynix is developing fabrication digital twins using Nvidia Omniverse libraries and OpenUSD pipelines to optimize complex semiconductor manufacturing environments.

competitor_articles.title: NAVER Expands AI Infrastructure With NVIDIA to Serve Surging Global AI Demand
competitor_articles.body: NVIDIA and NAVER announced an expansion of sovereign AI infrastructure using the NVIDIA DSX platform. NAVER will build AI factories at gigawatt scale, beginning with a 55-megawatt expansion at GAK Sejong data center in South Korea. The 55MW capacity is due online in 2027. The company then aims to expand its infrastructure overseas to 100MW within the same year and 200MW by 2028, targeting gigawatt-scale operations. The new DSX-powered cloud will expand Naver's GAK Sejong data center. NAVER will use NVIDIA full-stack AI platforms, models and software to advance regional AI models including next-generation HyperCLOVA X models, its Seoul World Model development, and agentic AI services. NAVER became the first Korean company joining the NVIDIA Nemotron Coalition, contributing to open model development across pretraining and post-training processes. NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang met with NAVER chairman Lee Hae-jin during the Korea visit. The companies also agreed to expand to Europe and the Middle East for joint AI infrastructure operations. The partnership focuses on implementing NemoClaw blueprints, with an AI Agent Platform launch planned for H2 2026.

competitor_articles.title: SK Telecom and NVIDIA Build AI Infrastructure to Power Korea's AI Innovation
competitor_articles.body: NVIDIA and SK Telecom announced that SK Telecom plans to build a gigawatt-scale AI Cloud in Korea using the NVIDIA DSX platform, with the first AI factory coming online in 2027. An AI Cloud is large-scale AI infrastructure comprised of AI factories that manufacture tokens — building blocks of intelligence — from data. SK Telecom's AI Cloud will be built on the NVIDIA DSX full-stack reference architecture of software, hardware and operations. SK Telecom's AI Cloud will power training, inference and agentic workloads including sovereign, physical and enterprise AI services for companies and industries across Korea, with the vision to expand to greater Asia. NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang noted: "Telecom networks are becoming national AI infrastructure." SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won stated the partnership gives them "full-stack AI infrastructure capabilities, from chips to data center operations." Beyond deployment, NVIDIA and SK Group committed to joint research on next-generation AI factory architecture, focusing on silicon-to-grid innovation and accelerated computing advancement. SK Telecom has already adopted NVIDIA Nemotron datasets for training sovereign AI models and applied NVIDIA Omniverse digital twins to semiconductor manufacturing optimization. Target capacity: 5 GW scale.
